title: Simple INNER JOIN
description: Write a query to get student names and their course titles using JOIN.
solutionSql: SELECT s.name, c.title FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id;
explanation: INNER JOIN combines rows from multiple tables based on matching conditions.

title: Join with Filter
description: Write a query to get teacher names and their course titles.
solutionSql: SELECT t.name, c.title FROM teachers t JOIN courses c ON t.id = c.teacher_id;
explanation: JOIN connects teachers to their courses using the teacher_id foreign key.

title: JOIN Types
description: Which JOIN returns only matching rows from both tables?
hints: It's the most common JOIN type
explanation: INNER JOIN returns only rows where there's a match in both tables.

title: Multiple JOINs
description: Write a query to get student names, course titles, and teacher names.
solutionSql: SELECT s.name, c.title, t.name as teacher_name FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id JOIN teachers t ON c.teacher_id = t.id;
explanation: Multiple JOINs connect several tables to get comprehensive data.

title: Fix JOIN Syntax
description: This query has an error. Fix it: SELECT * FROM students JOIN enrollments students.id = enrollments.student_id;
solutionSql: SELECT * FROM students JOIN enrollments ON students.id = enrollments.student_id;
explanation: JOIN requires the ON keyword to specify the join condition.
brokenQuery: SELECT * FROM students JOIN enrollments students.id = enrollments.student_id;

title: LEFT JOIN Example
description: Write a query to get all students and their courses, including students with no enrollments.
hints: Use LEFT JOIN to keep all students
solutionSql: SELECT s.name, c.title FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id LEFT JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id;
explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps all rows from the left table even if there's no match in the right table.
